positioning_check: Short interest 8.40% of float, 5.46 days to cover, up 2.3% month on month (MarketBeat quote page read 2026-10-26, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/commvault-systems-nasdaqcvlt-shares-gap-down-whats-next-2026-07-28/) - elevated but not a crowded short. Baseline: 25d skew -6.05 vol pts (calls richer than puts, 'upside paid'), put/call OI 0.58 on only 270 contracts total and a 19% ATM spread, so the skew is real but thin. Event-implied move 12.21%. Tape: +13.0% 20d, +9.5% 5d, 3.9% under the 52-week high, +122.6% off the 52-week low. Sell side: six October target raises (Mizuho 175->185 Oct 15, RBC 150->160 Oct 12, Guggenheim 175 Oct 19, Baird 160->180 Oct 23, Jefferies Hold 130->170 Oct 25, Cantor Hold 132->171 Oct 26; https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/cvlt/forecast/). Consensus Moderate Buy, 11 Buy/10 Hold, average target ~$163 below spot (MarketBeat).

findings.finding: Q2 subscription-revenue guide ($264-268M, midpoint $266M) sits BELOW the $267.0M Q1 actual, i.e. the company guided subscription revenue flat-to-down sequentially, and CVLT has beaten revenue in each of the last several quarters (Q1 $314.1M vs $310.5M consensus, EPS $1.42 vs $1.16; Q4 $311.7M vs $306.7M, EPS $1.28 vs $1.09), so a beat on subscription and total revenue (~$310M bar) of roughly 1% is the likely reported number.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats have been sold: July 2026 beat revenue and EPS and fell 19.7% on an unraised ARR guide; Oct 2025 -16.3%; Jan 2026 -31.1% on a net new ARR miss. Only Apr 2026 (+10.8%) and Jul 2025 (+18.3%) paid, both with ARR/guide news.
findings.why_not_priced: A revenue beat inside a conservative guide is expected by everyone; it is sized near zero because it lands inside what the company guided and the stock trades on net new ARR, not revenue. If the market were pricing more than a routine beat the skew would be the only sign, and it is.

findings.finding: The hardware/memory shortage that delayed CVLT's on-prem deals in Q1 tightened through the Jul-Sep quarter: Micron said on ~2026-10-01 that memory/storage supply will be considerably tighter in 2027-28 than 2026 with most of next year committed, Gartner cites some server prices up >125%; in Q1 CVLT's term-license revenue grew only 1% ($110.4M vs $109.3M) with >$100k transactions down 2%, and the CFO said term subscription lengths took a mid-single-digit sequential hit as customers weighed hardware plans, calling it 'a timing issue'. If the timing did not resolve in Q2, term-license revenue (recognised upfront) and the on-prem share of net new subscription ARR are at risk against the 'modest step-up' guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Net new ARR has been the line: Jan 2026 net new ARR miss -31.1%; July 2026 hardware-delay commentary plus unraised ARR guide -19.7%.
findings.why_not_priced: The company framed it as timing and the sell side has spent October raising targets; if the market were pricing a repeat on-prem shortfall, the Hold-rated brokers would not be lifting targets 30% and calls would not be bid over puts. Proxy: no CVLT or channel source has confirmed Q2 deals slipped.
findings.independence: Company-level mechanism from the 10-Q (term-license +1%, >$100k deals -2%): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001169561/000116956126000024/cvlt-20260630.htm and the call (https://newsable.asianetnews.com/markets/cvlt-stock-sees-worst-day-in-over-6-months-analyst-flags-limited-catalysts-after-q1-results-articleshow-gexg3dv). Netted against SaaS: SaaS ARR $424.3M +38%, about 40% of subscription ARR, is not hardware-gated and is what management said gives flexibility to offset.

findings.finding: The stock has re-run the July setup: +13.0% in 20 sessions and +9.5% in 5 into the print, 3.9% below the 52-week high, on six broker target raises in October including three from Hold/Sector Perform brokers (RBC to 160, Jefferies to 170, Cantor to 171) - into July it rose from ~$142 (Jul 24) to $149.46 and then fell 19.7% on an unraised ARR guide; peer Rubrik ran ~11% into its Aug 27 print, beat and raised everything, and fell 12% on decelerating net new cloud ARR.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: run-up into print, beat, -19.7%. Oct 2025: -16.3%. Apr 2026 from a depressed base (~$97): +10.8%. Elevated pre-print expectations have been punished 3 of the last 4 times on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Against the skew: calls are bid (-6.05 vol pts), which says the option market leans up. Why it may be wrong here: the call bid is the same momentum that the target raises reflect, on a thin chain (270 contracts OI, 19% ATM spread), and the July print showed this name's holders sell an unraised ARR guide regardless. Short interest at 8.4%/5.5 days is a squeeze mechanism on good news, which is why this is not larger.
findings.independence: Part of the run-up is sector beta: S&P software index at its highest since Nov 2025 on 2026-10-06 (https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2026-10-06/us-software-stocks-scale-fresh-2026-highs-as-ai-disruption-worries-fade); Rubrik analog: https://www.tikr.com/blog/rubrik-stock-fell-12-after-beating-earnings-heres-why-the-market-wasnt-satisfied

findings.finding: The 10-Q shows CVLT accrued $6.5M in Q1 as its 'current best estimate of amounts payable under a performance-based arrangement related to a strategic pricing and packaging initiative', with up to $3.0M more contingent on future performance outcomes - a consultant paid on measured results, i.e. the pricing/packaging change was live and producing outcomes by June, which supports ASP and subscription ARR in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on pricing; NRR was 114% in Q1. No reaction history on this line.
findings.why_not_priced: It sits in a 10-Q footnote and MD&A G&A walk, not in the release headline or any preview found; the wire treated it only as a non-GAAP add-back. If priced, previews would cite price-driven ARR uplift; none found. Inference: the fee size does not reveal the revenue uplift.
findings.independence: Same fee is disclosed in the release's non-GAAP reconciliation (same company, one fact): https://finviz.com/news/373277/commvault-announces-first-quarter-fiscal-2027-financial-results

findings.finding: Buybacks are back-loaded: FY27 guide is ~60% of $250-260M FCF (~$150-156M) but only $10.1M was repurchased in Q1, leaving ~$140M+ for Q2-Q4 against $239.9M authorised; a Q2 step-up in repurchases is likely disclosed in the release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No print has turned on buybacks; small.
findings.why_not_priced: Arithmetic on a published guide; largely priced, sized small accordingly.
findings.independence: FY27 buyback guide of ~60% of FCF in the Q1 release: https://finviz.com/news/373277/commvault-announces-first-quarter-fiscal-2027-financial-results
